body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo establishes a new milestone for global industry by organically linking core technologies across four key advanced sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Encompassing the achievements of Daegu Metropolitan City’s forward-looking industrial cultivation, leading domestic and international tech enterprises alongside promising startups will assemble to unveil next-generation, field-validated technologies poised to transform everyday life and industrial operations. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation initiatives, the event is set to serve as a pivotal exchange hub leading technological collaboration and innovation far beyond Asia.

Participating as an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, Ubergizmo is an influential consumer technology and innovative tech publication established in 2005 in Silicon Valley. Operating both English and Japanese editions, the outlet commands deep credibility among tech enthusiasts and Silicon Valley industry professionals. It delivers on-the-ground, in-depth reporting across premier international exhibitions, including CES in Las Vegas, MWC in Barcelona, IFA in Berlin, and CEATEC in Tokyo. Providing a balanced editorial perspective spanning consumer gadgets to deep-tech domains such as Physical AI, autonomous mobility, and robotics, Ubergizmo has consistently chronicled the international expansion of innovative South Korean enterprises. Visiting Daegu again following the 2025 event, Ubergizmo will vividly showcase promising Korean startups and breakthroughs to audiences across Silicon Valley and global markets. An advance interview was conducted with Eliane Fiolet, co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of Ubergizmo, to discuss the transition toward Physical AI and her expectations for FIX 2026.
1. Could you please introduce your media to a Korean audience?

Ubergizmo is an independent consumer technology media site that I co-founded with Hubert Nguyen in Silicon Valley in 2005. We publish mainly in English, with a Japanese edition, for a global audience of technology enthusiasts and industry readers. We cover gadgets, smartphones, AI, mobility, robotics, and the technologies behind them, with reviews, news, and on-site reporting from major shows such as CES in Las Vegas, MWC in Barcelona, IFA in Berlin, CEATEC in Tokyo, and FIX in Daegu.

Korean technology is a central part of our coverage. Our readers closely follow Korean companies and innovation, from consumer electronics to industrial technology and startups. That is why FIX in Daegu matters to us: it shows how Korean AI, mobility, and robotics move from research and factories into real products and services. For Korean readers, I hope Ubergizmo can help present that work clearly to a global audience.
2. What do you think about recent trends in industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

The clearest trend is the move from laboratory demos to systems that must work in factories, on roads, and in everyday life. In Korea, this is often called AX, or AI Transformation. Industrial AI, autonomous mobility, and robotics are converging into what we now call Physical AI.

Beyond artificial intelligence and computer vision, one of the key challenges in humanoid robotics is reproducing the dexterity, strength, and sensitivity of the human hand. For example, I visited the Younghyun Robotics booth at FIX 2025, where the company showcased its expertise in robotic hands and precision components. Over the past two years, I have seen advanced humanoid robots at every major technology show, from CES, MWC, and IFA to CEATEC and FIX, and progress now depends as much on high-quality actuators, joints, sensors, and hands as on AI software. In mobility and transportation, the key challenge now is to reach advanced levels of autonomous driving and continue developing energy-efficient electric vehicles, supported by a stronger grid, to achieve zero-emission mobility. Flying cars also interest me greatly.

body.x: 3. What major FIX 2026 topics does your audience have the most interest in?

Our audience is most interested in AI that leaves the lab and becomes useful products and services. For FIX 2026, that means industrial AI, autonomous mobility, EV technology, advanced sensing such as low-cost LiDARs, and robotics that people can experience directly.

Readers also closely follow humanoid and service robots, especially when the technology is practical enough for use in factories, logistics, healthcare, or daily life. Startups, the FIX Innovation Awards, and international partnerships matter too, because they show which companies are ready for global business. In short, our readers want concrete innovation with real industry and consumer impact that will improve their lives.
4. How was FIX 2025, and what do you expect from FIX 2026?

At FIX 2025, I was impressed by the quality and quantity of deep tech companies, and by the excellence of the award-winning innovations. The dominance of Physical AI and robotics was particularly impressive. The medical innovation was also very interesting to me, including IMsystem and A4LAB (more on those below).

I am excited to come back to Daegu. In May 2025, Daegu was designated an AI Robot Global Innovation Special Zone, with the city aiming to become Korea’s only core robot hub. For FIX 2026, under the theme “AI, Beyond Technology, Into Everyday Life,” I expect even more focus on practical AI in mobility, robotics, industry, and daily services, and I look forward to discovering this year’s outstanding companies.
5. What did you think of the FIX Innovation Awards press conference last year?

I was impressed by the quality of the companies presenting, and by how the awards highlighted real industrial impact, not only promising ideas. The medical innovation stood out to me in particular. IMsystem presented its micro medical robot for vascular interventional procedures, offering greater precision in minimally invasive surgery. A4LAB presented XAVE AIR, its surgical navigation system, which uses real-time imaging to improve surgical accuracy.

Both were among the Best of Innovation winners, showing how robotics and imaging can make complex procedures more precise and less invasive. More broadly, the press conference format was valuable because journalists could hear directly from the teams about the technology before the awards ceremony.

Both enterprises secured Best of Innovation honors, illustrating how robotics and advanced imaging can transform complex surgical workflows into more precise, non-invasive procedures. Structuring a dedicated press conference that allowed journalists to engage directly with the engineering and management teams ahead of the official ceremony proved exceptionally valuable and informative.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting on the frontline technological developments of the innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
